[repository-layout]
the score (committed)
created by `partitur init`; contains `runs/` and `work/` (run state and staging; neither is ever committed)
project cast override (committed or ignored, user's choice)
persistent repository-scoped state-mutation lock (§6)
AUTHORITATIVE — core-written only, never agent-writable
append-only event log (single writer: core)
rebuildable projection: score revision + hash, resolved cast pins, per-attempt enforcement record, artifact index
immutable score snapshots (see below)
the complete planned amendment.approved payload, written and fsynced BEFORE the prepare event (§6). Recovery replays this plan rather than recomputing one — an auto approval has no proposal record to rebuild from
immutable routed-proposal record, schema partitur/proposal-record+json;v=1 (§9). Decision-time re-validation replays the pipeline from the ORIGINAL operations, which a typed delta cannot reconstruct — the delta is lossy by design
durable destination for quarantined run files
the fully resolved cast used by this run
immutable artifact instances (identity and atomicity below); a retry never overwrites earlier evidence
immutable core-published review subject input (§4). It is outside every worktree and read-only to the performer; a retry or fallback on this movement revision reuses the same bytes
session hints, mode 0600 (see §4 privacy)
execution-driver lease (§6); absent when no driver runs
execution-authority checkpoint: current **epoch only** (§6). A PROJECTION of authority.granted / run.* events, like the manifest — rebuildable, never the authority itself. It does NOT hold the token: the token lives solely in driver.lease and its owner's memory, because a value that proves incarnation identity must not sit in a rebuildable file
sanitized vendor/adapter diagnostics (§4 privacy)
protocol trace
bounded criterion stdout capture (§7)
bounded criterion stderr capture (§7)
NON-AUTHORITATIVE staging — agent-writable
the attempt's output_dir (§5); artifacts are copied out of here into runs/.../artifacts/ and only the copy counts
default temporary-file directory for criterion commands (§7)
user-global cast override

[score-example]
schema version
bumped only by amendments
draft | finalized
finalized user intent — prose, in the user's language
project facts the user supplied (optional)
the one movement allowed to run while status: draft
DRAFT gate — finalization requires every entry
resolved or explicitly waived
explicit waiver, recorded forever
two separate concepts — see below
write-basic-tests | pass-existing-tests | none work intent; forwarded to briefs as brief.verification_expectation. 'none' is always explicit. NOT ship policy.
which evidence `apply` demands — require XOR waived
non-empty, duplicate-free subset of {verified, approved, reviewed}
optional; closed enum, §8
required iff apply_gate is not waived; forbidden when waived. The run's terminal sink — §8. — or, for a deliberately ungated run — expectation: intent: none apply_gate: waived: true reason: "spike; will be rewritten"   # non-empty reason mandatory
logical roles — never vendor or model names
never receives a write grant
units of work; DAG via `needs`; each played by one part
runs while status: draft — see DRAFT phase contract
kind: change_set is CORE-SYNTHESIZED — the performer never
emits it as an artifact; the core captures it from the worktree. See §5.
a movement with a repo_write grant MUST have ≥1
hard criterion or human_gate: always
explicit, unique within the movement — marks bind to it
verification.final_movement — the run's terminal sink:
transitively needs every non-draft movement, has no
downstream, and never holds repo_write
apply_gate.require is [verified, reviewed], so this
movement must carry ≥1 hard AND ≥1 review criterion
(achievability, §8)
typed requirement: this findings artifact must
exist and be well-formed
always | on_contested | never
unordered union of positive glob patterns; duplicates are a compiler error and order carries no semantics
v0.2 accepts only an empty list; non-empty values are rejected until a typed side-effect registry is specified
active execution time only — adapter runs, acceptance, retries, fallbacks. WAITING_HUMAN and stopped time are excluded. Consumed time is persisted via journal events; each attempt receives the remainder at its start.
quality-retry budget per movement — see §3
off | envelope; default off. envelope = only provably-monotone changes inside the bounds below are auto-approved (§9); everything else waits for a human.

[adapter-methods]
protocol 2. An OPEN list of feature tokens, not a closed enum: a closed enum would need a bump for every future token, which is the problem negotiation exists to solve. A core ignores tokens it does not know; an adapter advertises only what it implements. No tokens are defined in v0.2; absent or empty means none.
what the adapter/vendor agent actually enforces. Absent booleans decode as false — fail closed.
confines writes AND reads to granted paths
can run with all repository writes disabled
can disable data-plane network
can disable command execution entirely — true only if EVERY command-execution route is closed
can deny repository reads
the score projection for this part — the intent,
constraints, and invariants it needs (per CONCEPT)
omitted entirely when the score omits it (§2 defaults) — never sent as ""
user intent, forwarded to relevant parts; whether it
was met is judged by acceptance, never by the adapter
deterministic projection computed by the core from goal, finalized resolutions, and policy — not a separate score field
this movement's declared outputs — the only
artifact ids the attempt may emit
`instance_id` is delivered, not just hashed: A.5 binds it, so a performer and the core must agree on which instance this is
diagnostics from prior failed attempts (see §7). Delivered like
any other input — a readable path and a hash — because a bare
artifact id is not something a performer can open
read-only, inside the attempt's readable area
sha256: raw bytes, so tampering is detectable
read-only; never applied to the base
tagged union; every entry carries `kind`
see the blocking handshake below for the closed variants
the attempt worktree (see §5)
always-writable artifact area (see §5)
remaining at attempt start, INTEGER MILLISECONDS. Not `active_wall_clock_min`: the score declares the cap in minutes but the remainder is tracked and compared in ms (§6), and a minutes-only field could not carry it losslessly
only the namespace matching this adapter's id
present when outcome = failed
present when outcome = waiting_human; an attempt may raise several questions and blocks on all of them
transport-level outcome only — the adapter NEVER judges success; the core runs acceptance.

[event-notifications]
path must be inside output_dir; the core immediately copies the file into runs/<id>/artifacts/ (see §1 atomicity) and treats only that immutable copy as recorded
structured amendment (§2 format); core
validates; id is stable within the attempt
see blocking handshake below

[reserved-inputs]
supplied to any movement whose `may_propose`
is true (§2)
a proposal's base_revision MUST equal this
... and its base_hash MUST equal this — semantic (partitur/score, Appendix A), which is what makes the proposal stale-checkable (§9)
the canonical JSON score at that revision
supplied to any movement declaring a review
criterion
the CORE-OBSERVED tree — a review performer cannot compute this itself, especially with no shell
